Kuvitus: syysilta maantiellä kuusimetsän: Illustration: an autumn evening on a country road in the middle of a spruce forest. A car with its headlights on approaches from the left. On the right side of the road is a moose warning sign, and behind it a moose steps from the edge of the forest onto the road in front of the car. The distance between the car and the moose is short compared with the distance the car needs to stop.
Kaksi tietä päällekkäin, matkat mittakaa: Two roads one above the other, distances to scale, cars not. In both, the driver notices the danger at the dashed line. At the top the speed is 50 kilometres per hour: a green reaction distance of 13.9 metres and a brown braking distance of 10.7 metres, 24.6 metres in total. At the bottom the speed is 100 kilometres per hour: the reaction distance is twice as long, 27.8 metres, and the braking distance four times as long, 42.9 metres, 70.6 metres in total. The reaction time is 1.0 seconds and the deceleration 9.0 metres per second squared. Below, a tape measure in metres.
Vasemmalla tilannekuva: auto jarruttaa v: On the left a picture of the situation: a car brakes on a horizontal road, the brake lights are on. Above the car a blue velocity arrow points forwards to the right and an orange acceleration arrow points backwards to the left. On the right the free-body diagram of the car, the car drawn as a rectangle: the weight G from the centre downwards, the normal force N of the road from the lower surface upwards, as long as the weight, and the friction F mu of the road from the rear corner of the lower surface backwards, almost as long as the weight. Friction is the only horizontal force.
Kaavakuva, pyöristetyt esimerkkiarvot: m: Schematic graph, rounded example values: the speed of a passenger in a frontal collision from a speed of 50 kilometres per hour. On the horizontal axis the time 0–0.12 seconds, on the vertical axis the speed 0–16 metres per second. Blue line: a passenger wearing a belt slows down steadily with the car from 13.9 metres per second to zero in 0.10 seconds. Brown line: without a belt the passenger keeps moving at 13.9 metres per second until 0.090 seconds, hits the interior of the car and stops in 0.010 seconds. The change in speed is the same in both.
Kaavakuva (t, v)-kuvaajasta, ei lukuarvo: Schematic of a (t, v) graph, no numerical values. The speed stays at the value v_0 during the reaction time t_r, so the graph is horizontal, and under it is a green rectangle whose area is the reaction distance s_r = v_0 t_r. Then the speed falls in a straight line to zero during the braking time t_b, and under the graph is a brown triangle whose area is the braking distance s_b = half of v_0 t_b. The magnitude of the slope of the line is the deceleration a.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, pyöristetyt esime: Graph to scale, rounded example values for a 75 kilogram passenger from a speed of 50 kilometres per hour. On the horizontal axis the time 0–0.12 seconds, on the vertical axis the average force 0–120 kilonewtons. A low blue rectangle: with a belt the force is about 10 kilonewtons for 0.10 seconds. A narrow, tall brown rectangle: without a belt the force is about 100 kilonewtons for 0.010 seconds. The areas of the rectangles are equal.
